claim: The weekly summary counts every event in exactly one week.
why: The week windows are half-open, so no event is counted twice, and the default local run counts all 5 events once. But the first week and the number of weeks come from SUMMARY_START and SUMMARY_WEEKS, which the deployed job sets and the repo does not show. Whether every event falls inside the deployed window cannot be settled from the repo, so a confirmation on the strength of the default run overreaches.

deciding.note: no event can land in two windows
the default local run counts all 5 events once
the deployed window is outside the repo

root.claim: The weekly summary counts every event in exactly one week.

atoms.claim: No event is counted in two weeks.
atoms.evidence: weekly.py uses start <= d < end, so the windows are half-open and a Monday belongs only to the week it starts.

atoms.claim: With the default settings every event is counted exactly once.
atoms.evidence: python3 main.py prints [2, 2, 1] 5 5, so the sum equals the number of events.

atoms.claim: The deployed window set by SUMMARY_START and SUMMARY_WEEKS covers every event.
atoms.evidence: settings.py reads both values from the environment and the README says the deployed job sets its own; those values are not in the repo. SUMMARY_WEEKS=2 drops the 2025-01-20 event.
